item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
…this is silly.
This man gains access to deep foundation secrets, and the truth behind the scip he’s been researching, not due to the many years he spent trying to discover how to open the lock, but by solving a scooby-doo-esque riddle left by his previous coworker.
Also, he needs the help of an overheard conversation to realise that he should ask a Sumerian about the immortal Sumerian famine. He doesn’t even need to realise it’s referring to Abel, he just needs to ask Cain.
I like the idea, but this is goofy to the extreme.
-1.

item.title: !rtd
item.content:encoded:
In ancient Greek cult-practice and literature, a nekyia (Ancient Greek: ἡ νέκυια) is a "rite by which ghosts were called up and questioned about the future," i.e., necromancy. A nekyia is not necessarily the same thing as a katabasis.

Wikipedia article for Nekyia.
